sentences: I measure the length of a cockroach's antennae with a ruler and note the number in my log.
I count the veins in a dragonfly's wing under a magnifying glass and write the total down.
I observe a grasshopper extending its hind legs to jump from a blade of grass to the soil.
I examine the coiled proboscis of a butterfly with a hand lens and measure its uncoiled length.
I note the hexagonal facets on a fly's compound eye using a dissecting microscope.
I press on the hard elytra of a beetle to test the stiffness of its exoskeleton.
I watch a cicada nymph climb a tree trunk and split its old skin to emerge as an adult.
I record the dates when a monarch caterpillar forms a chrysalis and later emerges as a butterfly.
I find a raft of mosquito eggs floating on stagnant water and count the individual eggs.
I collect aquatic larvae from a stream with a fine net and place them in a tray.
I keep a silk cocoon in a jar and check it every morning for signs of change.
I map the tunnels of an ant colony in the garden by pouring a thin stream of water.
I follow a solitary wasp as it hunts for a spider among the leaves.
I see a bee transfer pollen from a flower's stamen to its pistil and then fly away.
I observe a praying mantis catch a cricket and hold it with its spiked forelegs.
I note a parasitic wasp inserting its ovipositor into a caterpillar to lay eggs inside.
I watch a bombardier beetle release a hot chemical spray from its abdomen when disturbed.
I detect the pheromone trail left by ants by following their line to a food source.
I track the southward flight path of a monarch butterfly using a pair of binoculars.
I sift through leaf litter to find springtails and other tiny insects living in the soil.
